Frontend end-to-end 2-browser-context flow PASS: Metered TURN credentials returned (turn:true, valid turn: URL w/ username+credential), demo's call presence shows up as 'Demo memulai panggilan' incoming for budi, demo's own /api/calls/incoming excludes self, FriendCallRing banner appears on budi's /home within <20s, friend-call-accept navigates budi to /chat/<dmId> and auto-opens RealtimeMeeting, both clients show rtm-humans '1/1 teman terhubung' within ~1s, peer-mute-<budiId> button toggles bg-[#EF4444] on/off and tile dims, rtm-leave on budi drops demo's count to 0/1, demo on his own call page shows NO self friend-call-ring, decline path dismisses the ring and it does NOT reappear during the next ≥12s while the caller stays in the room, final /api/calls/incoming is [] for both after leaving. /chat, /friends and badge-chat regression all OK.
critical_code_review_comments: rtc.py ice_servers(): no server-side caching of the Metered TURN credentials — each ICE fetch calls the upstream https://<app>.metered.live/.../credentials endpoint. On a flaky or rate-limited TURN provider this will fail an entire call startup; consider caching for ~5–10 minutes (TURN creds TTL is typically hours). Also catch httpx.ReadTimeout explicitly if needed.

rtc.py call_presence(): doesn't require the user to actually be the caller — any participant can call /presence, which is correct by design, but there's no payload-size or rate limit, so a client bug could spam presence writes and keep the ring alive. Low risk.

rtc.py incoming_calls(): the ISO-string cutoff comparison assumes every active_call entry stores UTC isoformat the same way call_presence writes it. OK today since both use now_iso(); fragile if a future call site stores a different format.

FriendCallRing.jsx polls every 5s with no exponential backoff/jitter — fine for small deployments but every signed-in user hitting /calls/incoming every 5s will become notable at scale. Consider page-visibility pause and 15s when hidden.

FriendCallRing.jsx `startRing` creates an AudioContext but on strict browser autoplay policies the context may be in 'suspended' state until user gesture — the first ring will be silent. Consider calling ac.resume() in a user-gesture handler (e.g. first click anywhere) and attaching a visual cue regardless.

FriendCallRing.jsx: `dismissed` is in a useRef `Set` so it doesn't survive page reload. If a user hard-refreshes while a friend's call is still live, the previously-declined call will ring again. Minor UX.

RealtimeMeeting.jsx: presence heartbeat only fires when humans.length > 0 (correct), but the beat() call runs even if the mesh fails to start (no catch). If `mesh.start()` throws before `window.__oryntixInCall = true`, cleanup won't unset the presence. Would need an explicit /call/leave on connect() error path.

RealtimeMeeting.jsx togglePeerMute: setState closure also mutates DOM audio elements inside the updater — this is a side-effect in a setter which may run twice under React strict mode and could double-add/remove tracks. Low-risk because add()/remove() of the same MediaStream is idempotent for most mixer impls, but worth refactoring to a useEffect.
